title: act-on-weather / Pipeline
description: The delivery path, left to right: accepted -> outbox -> broker -> consumer -> database, then enrichment and freshness. This is the dashboard that shows whether the no-data-loss guarantee (M11) is being kept. Read the top row first: it is the only part that can show data at risk. Core panel types only (timeseries, stat, bargauge) -- a plugin panel would have to be downloaded from grafana.com, and this stack has no route out.

panels.title: Outbox: accepted records not yet published, by producer
panels.description: Where the guarantee begins. A record is fsynced into the producer's outbox -- a named volume, so it survives the container -- before the caller is told 'accepted'. Pending means accepted and durable but not yet on the broker. A spike during a broker restart is the system working; a plateau that never drains is not.

panels.title: Oldest unpublished record, by producer (seconds) -- AowOutboxStuck fires above 300s
panels.description: The M11 signal, and the single most important number on this dashboard. It is how long the longest-stranded accepted record has been waiting to reach the broker. Zero means nothing is pending. It is not data loss -- the row is durable -- but it is the window in which loss would become possible if the volume were destroyed too, so it is the honest measure of the guarantee's exposure.

panels.title: Publish failures to the broker (failures/second, by producer)
panels.description: Counts attempts that did not reach RabbitMQ. A producer with a readable outbox and no failures shows zero. If its outbox cannot be read, the series disappears rather than claiming zero. A failed publish leaves the row pending for retry.

panels.title: Messages published to the exchange (messages/second, by routing key)
panels.description: The other side of the outbox: what actually left. Compare with the consumer-throughput panel below -- a sustained gap between the two is the queue filling up, which is exactly what AowQueueBacklog watches.

panels.title: Queue depth: aow.ingest (messages waiting) -- AowQueueBacklog fires above 500
panels.description: From the broker's own exporter, not from the consumer. That is deliberate and it is the whole point: a consumer that has crashed cannot report how far behind it is, and that is precisely when this number matters. Note the series comes from Prometheus' /metrics/detailed scrape -- the aggregated endpoint publishes rabbitmq_queue_messages with NO queue label, summing the ingest and dead-letter queues together.

panels.title: Dead-lettered messages in aow.dlq -- `make dlq` to inspect, `make redrive` to replay
panels.description: Messages the consumer rejected enough times to be quarantined. They are parked, NOT lost: the queue is durable, and writes are idempotent, so replaying one that did land the first time cannot double-count it. Anything above zero for five minutes fires AowDeadLetters.

panels.title: Time since the consumer last handled a message (seconds)
panels.description: Includes stored, duplicate and rejected deliveries. 'No delivery recorded' means the current consumer has not handled a message, or Prometheus cannot scrape it; check the scrape targets. Idle is normal when queue depth is zero.

panels.title: Consumer outcomes (messages/second: stored, duplicate, rejected)
panels.description: The three things that can happen to a message, and all three are worth seeing. 'duplicate' is not an error -- delivery is at-least-once and writes are idempotent, so duplicates are the guarantee working, and a redrive should produce a visible burst of them. 'rejected' sustained is AowConsumerRejecting and usually means a producer and consumer disagree about a schema.

panels.title: Message processing time p95, by routing key (seconds)
panels.description: Measured from the consumer picking a message up to the database commit that precedes the ack. Ack after commit is what makes at-least-once true, so this number is also the width of the window in which a crash produces a redelivery rather than a loss.

panels.title: Enrichment backlog: recommendations awaiting the model
panels.description: 'pending' is waiting to be worded. 'deferred' is a deliberate decision, not a failure: the rule engine scores all 18 activities per city-day because that is free, and only the top ENRICH_TOP_N are sent to a CPU-bound model -- the rest are stored deferred with their deterministic score intact. A deferred row is still a complete, usable recommendation.

panels.title: Enrichment outcomes (requests/second: ready, invalid, unavailable)
panels.description: 'unavailable' is the model server being unreachable; 'invalid' is the model answering with something the grounding check refuses. Different causes, different fixes, so they are different alerts: AowModelUnavailable and AowEnrichmentFailing. In both cases the recommendation stays pending rather than being stored with wording nobody verified -- refusing is the designed behaviour.

panels.title: Model wording time p95 (seconds per recommendation)
panels.description: One CPU generation from the local 1.7B model. Several seconds is normal here and is why ENRICH_TOP_N exists at all. If this and the API's p95 rise together, the model server is contended and LLM_PARALLEL is the knob -- compose.yml explains why it is 2.

panels.title: Time since the last successful ingestor run, by source (seconds)
panels.description: Time since this ingestor process last accepted records, not the age of the source data. 'Never succeeded' means the current process has no successful run. Replaying an old snapshot resets this timer but does not make the weather newer. Check Data coverage in the app for source as-of dates.

panels.title: Ingestion attempts since ingestor start, by source and outcome
panels.description: Counts ingestor attempts since this process started. A snapshot replay is one attempt; live mode counts one per city. A short-lived `make refresh` container cannot be scraped and reports its outcome in the app's Update data page. A failed attempt accepted no records and must be retried while connected.
